episodes.title: Who Has the Power?
episodes.description: Introduce government by asking who makes decisions about laws and public services.

episodes.title: Elite vs. Pluralist Theory
episodes.description: This episode dives into some of the theories about political influence throughout US history, with a special focus on Elite and Pluralist Theory.

episodes.title: Life, Liberty, and Natural Rights
episodes.description: We’ll cover foundational philosophical beliefs on governance and see how they’re reflected in our current view of the government’s role in society.

episodes.title: The Messy Articles of Confederation
episodes.description: Examine the Articles of Confederation as the system that preceded the US Constitution.

episodes.title: A Case of Federal vs. State Power
episodes.description: US federalism can lead to some controversial issues when the national government and the individual states want to have different policies.

episodes.title: Pros and Cons of Federalism
episodes.description: In this episode, we’ll dive deeper into how policy differences have polarized our states in order to examine the pros and cons of federalism.

episodes.title: Are My Civil Rights Being Violated?
episodes.description: In today’s episode, we’ll be discussing civil rights and how the court system within the United States determines if a law is discriminatory or not.

episodes.title: Boosting Federal Power Post-Civil War
episodes.description: In this episode we examine the contradiction of slavery being legal in a nation purportedly founded on inalienable rights.

episodes.title: When the Bill of Rights Didn’t Apply
episodes.description: Explore how constitutional civil liberties came to constrain state governments as well as the federal government.

episodes.title: Where do You Challenge the Government?
episodes.description: Consider historical efforts to secure rights and what they can teach us about present debates.

episodes.title: In the Shadows of the Constitution
episodes.description: Explore the Supreme Court’s interpretation of civil liberties through its debates over the constitutional right to privacy.

episodes.title: Where do Political Beliefs Come From?
episodes.description: Explore the sources of political opinions.

episodes.title: How Polls Influence Politics
episodes.description: In today’s episode, we’ll be breaking down what factors make a poll scientific and discussing the importance of polls in US politics!

episodes.title: Why Doesn’t Everyone Vote?
episodes.description: In today’s episode, we’ll be reviewing what makes someone more or less likely to vote by examining voter turnout in the US.

episodes.title: Is Voting Rational or Emotional?
episodes.description: Explore the choices and considerations involved in deciding how to vote.

episodes.title: How do Primary Elections Work?
episodes.description: Explore primary and general elections, campaigning, and fundraising to understand how candidates reach the ballot and win office.

episodes.title: How the Media Shapes Democracy
episodes.description: Today we’ll be discussing the different ways that news and media outlets can make their news more influential, and how this affects our democracy.

episodes.title: The History of Media and Politics
episodes.description: Explore competition between traditional news sources and social media.

episodes.title: Where are All the Party Options?
episodes.description: This episode looks at how the two-party system emerged and why the current US election system keeps us in it.

episodes.title: Is My Book Club an Interest Group?
episodes.description: One of the main channels of communication between the public and the government is interest groups.

episodes.title: Who are the People Who Represent Us?
episodes.description: When we elect our legislative representatives, we’re electing someone to stand in our place to make decisions on our behalf.

episodes.title: How Does Congress “Work”?
episodes.description: Explore how congressional leaders, party leaders, and committee chairs coordinate the process of creating and passing legislation.

episodes.title: Why is the President on Social Media?
episodes.description: Explore how presidents draw power from public support and how the relationship between presidents and the public has evolved.

episodes.title: It’s Not You, It’s the Electoral College
episodes.description: Explore the Electoral College’s role in selecting the US president.

episodes.title: Why People Hate the Supreme Court
episodes.description: Examine the role and significance of the Supreme Court and the judicial branch.

episodes.title: There Are 90k Governments in the US?!?!
episodes.description: Explore the many levels and forms of government across the United States.

episodes.title: What is Bureaucracy Good For?
episodes.description: Explore the bureaucracy beyond its common negative associations.

episodes.title: Is There Really a “Deep State”?
episodes.description: Explore ways to investigate and evaluate what government is doing.

episodes.title: Public Policy in the US
episodes.description: Today, we’ll review the different types of US public policy and how Robin Hood might have felt about them.

episodes.title: Our Evolving Foreign Policy
episodes.description: Trace the debate over US involvement abroad, beginning with Washington’s preference for avoiding foreign entanglements.
